items.item_text: High School Diploma
Is exposed to excessive noise: Yes
Is around moving machinery: Yes
Is exposed to marked changes in temperature and/or humidity: Yes
Drives motorized equipment: Yes
Dust: Yes

Two years of experience in a storeroom or warehouse in the performance of work involving the receipt, storage, and issuance of a variety of supplies, material, and equipment, or a combination of experience and education/training.
Experience in maintenance and repair operations.
Experience operating a forklift
Experience in computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS) such as FAMIS 360.
Experience in Oracle Procurement.

Inventory & Material Management: Coordinates the physical storage and organization of a material and inventory program valued at approximately $825K. Coordinates with the Procurement & Warehouse Analyst to identify materials that need to be added to the program or removed as stock utilization becomes low to ensure the availability of materials for Maintenance Repair Operations (MRO). Determines space requirements, stock control methods, physical organization of materials and warehouse operations. Coordinates cycle and inventory counts; organizes material kits for pick up; stocks shelves with materials. Orders standard inventorial commodities; coordinates with vendors for price and product comparisons; verifies receipt of goods to facilitate payment. (40% time)

Logistics & Receipt: Manages the receipt of goods by unloading, counting, and inspecting incoming stock against purchase orders to verify items and quantities. Tracks, monitors and manages handling freight claims, damage reports, and back orders. (15% time)

Compliance & Safety: Maintains the storeroom in a secure, clean, and safe condition. Ensures all warehouse activities comply with internal audit requirements, UCR/UCOP policies, and AQMD regulations regarding hazardous waste and fuel usage. (15% time)

Record Keeping: Utilizes the computerized maintenance management system to facilitate reorders, restock, and shopping carts of inventory warehouse. Makes daily entries of goods received and report the issuance of outgoing items. Supports FS Staff to be trained on using the CMMS and inventory module. Collaborates with the Procurement & Warehouse Analyst to recommend modifications to the CMMS to support multiple warehouse sites and compliance with inventory records. (15% time)

Customer Service: Serves as the primary point of contact for the warehouse; ensures professional, cooperative partnerships are built, maintained and managed for internal and external customers. Investigate and resolve complaints regarding the quantity or quality of goods received to ensure departmental satisfaction. Other duties as assigned; may be tasked to assist with supporting in other administrative and customer service tasks. (15% time)
Required to hold valid driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program.
Read/Comprehend: Constantly

Climb: Frequently
Other: Lift up to 50 lbs.

Work in a safe and responsible manner while not putting self or others at risk. Comply with applicable policies and procedures and regulations, using personal safety gear, observing warning signs, learning about potential hazards and reporting unsafe conditions. Must be able to exert well-paced mobility of up to four hours in length and stand continuously throughout an eight hour shift on uncarpeted surfaces. Must be able to move 30 pounds frequently and 50 pounds occasionally following proper safety guidelines. Must be able to stand, walk, climb, stoop, push, pull, reach and crouch for extended periods of time, as required to complete job assignments. Ability to work in temperature extremes, continuous noise and physical environments.
Knowledge of and experience with modern warehousing and retail merchandising practices.
Skill to work in a team environment with student employees and maintain quality control with inexperienced workers. Ability to give and follow explicit directions and carry out instructions.
Skill in entering, transcribing, recording, or maintaining information in an electronic format.

Communication skills sufficient to effectively and diplomatically communicate with vendors, peers, supervisors, managers and university staff. Ability to read, speak and understand English sufficient to determine and carry out job duties and communicate with supervisors, co-workers, vendors, and customers.
Skill to change priorities at a moments notice as to not impact operations when problems arise. Able to work in a fast paced and occasionally stressful work environment.
General knowledge of standard warehouse procedures. Knowledge of general receiving procedures.
Skill in accurate record keeping with strict attention to detail, organizing tasks, documents and materials with efficiency and accuracy.
Knowledge of and experience with inventory control functions, including experience in physical inventory counts, receiving and storage of materials and first in first out (FIFO) methods.
Skill in adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing whole numbers, fractions, and decimals, computing ratios, rates and percentages.
Knowledge of and experience with warehouse and maintenance and repair operations (MRO) related inventory.
General knowledge of storekeeping methods and practices including packing and shipping a wide variety of commodities.
